blocks.text: Paint Sheens: How to Choose the Right Finish

Choosing a paint color is the fun part, but picking the right finish is where many homeowners get stuck. Sheen, or the level of gloss in your paint, plays a huge role in both the look and performance of your walls. Whether you’re painting a cozy bedroom or a busy hallway, the right paint sheen can enhance aesthetics, improve durability, and make cleaning easier.

At Black Pearl Painters, we don’t just help our Pacific Northwest clients choose the perfect colors, we guide them through the best paint types for every room, based on traffic, lighting, and style preferences. In this post, we’ll walk you through a complete paint sheens guide so you can feel confident in your choices, and enjoy long-lasting, beautiful results.
What are Paint Sheens, Exactly?

Paint sheens refers to how shiny or reflective the surface is once the paint dries. Higher sheen paints have more gloss and reflect more light. Lower sheen paints have a more matte, velvety look and absorb more light.
Your choice affects:

items: How the color appears in different lighting
How easy it is to clean
How well imperfections are hidden or revealed
The overall vibe and style of a room

blocks.text: Let’s break down the main types of sheen, from ultra-flat to super-shiny, and when and where to use them.
1. Flat or Matte Finish
Best for:

items: Rooms with lots of wall imperfections

blocks.text: Flat and matte paints have little to no sheen, giving them a smooth, elegant look that’s perfect for spaces where you want a calm, cozy atmosphere. They’re excellent at hiding surface flaws, like small cracks or uneven textures, making them ideal for older homes or ceilings with visible seams.

However, flat paint is the least washable of all sheens. It can scuff and mark more easily, so it’s not the best choice for high-traffic areas or homes with pets and kids, unless you don’t mind frequent touch-ups.
2. Eggshell Finish
Best for:

Eggshell is one of the most popular finishes, and for good reason. It has just a touch of sheen, offering a nice balance between flat and glossy. It’s more durable and washable than matte, but still soft enough to keep walls looking smooth and rich.
Why we love it: Eggshell gives walls a warm, inviting glow while offering some stain resistance. It works beautifully in spaces that see regular, but not rough, use.
3. Satin Finish
Best for:

Satin is a step up in shine and cleanability, making it a great option for moisture-prone or high-traffic spaces. It resists mildew and stands up well to scrubbing; perfect for busy households or areas that need regular wipe-downs.

It reflects more light than eggshell, which adds brightness to darker rooms. Just be aware: satin finishes can slightly highlight surface imperfections, so great prep work is key; something Black Pearl Painters always provides.
4. Semi-Gloss Finish
Best for:

items: Bathrooms and kitchens (for a little extra shine)

blocks.text: Semi-gloss is durable, moisture-resistant, and very easy to clean. It’s a top choice for areas that get touched or bumped frequently, like baseboards, door frames, and cabinet doors.

It has a noticeable sheen, so it will draw attention to the areas it covers. That makes it ideal for architectural details you want to highlight, but less ideal for rough or uneven surfaces unless they’ve been smoothed out properly.

blocks.text: 5. Gloss (or High-Gloss) Finish
Best for:

High-gloss is the most reflective finish, and the most durable. It creates a glass-like sheen that’s dramatic and sleek, perfect for a bold modern look. It’s not widely used on walls but can be striking on built-ins, stair railings, or as a statement trim in a high-style space.
That said, it will magnify any surface imperfection, so proper sanding and priming are essential.
